incident-bot: Pager fired for service=az7-fabric-controlplane at 2026-03-10T08:12:01Z. symptom=heartbeat-loss, impact=serve-degraded

pagerduty-bot: INC-4242 created and routed to oncall-sre. Escalation policy: control-plane -> infra-sre -> eng-pager.

Marta: saw the PD page. quick check: are we seeing instance evictions or just control-plane heartbeats?

Ryan: telemetry shows control-plane heartbeats missed across multiple hosts in az7 starting ~08:10. agent logs show TCP RST to kube-apiserver from fabric node mgmt.

Tariq: acked on PD. I'm taking primary. pinging infra to confirm network fabric flaps. @Ryan can you grab the cluster health output?

Ryan: pasted cluster status: 
```
kubectl get nodes --all-namespaces | grep az7
node-az7-01   NotReady  2m  kubelet-notready
node-az7-02   NotReady  1m
node-az7-03   Ready     10m
```

Marta: customer-facing impact: Dedicated pools pinned to az7 show 5-10% 5xx increase; hosted traffic auto-failed to az8 but some sticky sessions still hit az7. CS already alerted via support queue.

Tariq: checking routing logs. It looks like the smart-router sent failover signals but some long-lived websocket connections didn't migrate. Those are causing 503s.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: escalation in 5m if not acknowledged by secondary.

Marta: we should activate fallback policy full failover for the affected pools. Will need to coordinate with deployment control to force divert and drain az7 worker backends.

Elaine: I'm on the infra channel working with fabric team. There's a noisy NIC on fabric-switch-az7-4; vendor tickets inbound. We can accelerate divert but need approval for sticky session reset for a subset of customers.

Mike: tagging in network: switching fabric-switch-az7-4 to emergency-paths=on to stop blackholing heartbeats. Doing now.
Mike: done. I see heartbeats recovering on nodes 01 and 02. kubelet reporting Ready for node-az7-01 at 08:22.

Ryan: service metrics returning to normal, error rate dropping from 8% -> 1.2% over 6 minutes. Websocket reconnect churn still being observed for clients with pinned affinity.

Customer Success: we got a handful of priority-2 tickets. Most customers recovered after reconnect. Logged: CS-8790, CS-8791. We should send an initial impact note.

Tariq: handoff: I'm going to stabilize for 15m then hand to Elaine for postmortem. Current action items:
- Confirm fabric switch fix is durable (Mike + network)
- Run routing dry-run to ensure no more sticky hits to az7 (Ryan)
- Collate affected customer list for CS (Marta + Customer Success)
- Collect kube and fabric logs for 08:05-08:25 window (Elaine)

Marta: quick command to force-drain backend pool for riskier customers (only if recovery stalls):
```
redwood-ctl routing divert --pool dedicated-az7 --target az8 --grace 30
```

Tariq: don't run that yet. monitoring looks good. We will keep the command ready.

incident-bot: Note: INC-4242 status=acknowledged, primary=Tariq, escalated=false.

Elaine: taking oncall at 08:35 handoff. I'll coordinate postmortem and customer impact note. tagging follow-ups in #postmortems.

Marta: filed a quick customer impact blurb for CS to send out, focusing on transient websocket reconnects for pinned pools; no data loss.

Tariq: final check: latency and token-costs normal, no abnormal autoscaler activity. closing the immediate response. If errors spike again, reopen PD.

pagerduty-bot: INC-4242 status=resolved by Tariq at 2026-03-10T08:37:02Z (note: will auto-close in 1h unless reopened).

Elaine: post-incident tasks assigned: network to confirm hardware replacement schedule, infra to add extra routing fallback, eng to add eval for sticky session migration. I'll draft the postmortem and include timeline.

Marta: thanks all. good job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:

Ryan: follow-up: adding temporary alert to detect elevated websocket reconnect rate per-az so we catch this earlier.

Customer Success: sending update to affected customers now.

incident-bot: Thread closed for live mitigation. Archive to incidents log.
